title: Cypress
description: End-to-end testing with automatic waiting and time travel.

data.text: Cypress runs in the same loop as your application. It provides automatic waiting, time travel debugging, and a powerful GUI.

data.title: Cypress test

data.text: End-to-End Tests That Run in a Real Browser

Cypress drives a real browser from the test process, so it can see the DOM, network, and application just as a user would. Commands such as `cy.visit`, `cy.get`, and `cy.click` are queued and retried, and `cy.intercept` stubs or spies on network calls.

data.title: A login flow with an intercept

data.text: Repeated setup such as logging in is extracted into a custom command in `support/commands.ts`, keeping tests readable. Fixtures under `cypress/fixtures` hold canned data. `cy.session` caches a login across tests so the suite does not sign in for every case.

data.title: A custom login command
Interview angle: the testing pyramid
data.text: Unit tests are fast and numerous, integration tests cover how units combine, and end-to-end tests confirm the whole path but are slow and flaky. Cypress sits at the top, so good suites keep the end-to-end count small and cover the critical paths — login, checkout, the main workflow. Saying where it fits beats saying it is the best tool.
